content.thinking:
I'm reading through this paper on HPT-JT syndrome, noting the two families described with renal hamartomas and cystic kidney disease, and the proportions of affected individuals showing HPT, jaw tumors, and renal lesions in each pedigree.

Now I'm working through the genetic linkage analysis, where twenty microsatellite markers in the HRPT2 region plus MEN1 and MEN2 markers were typed, showing linkage to five markers in 1q21-q32 while excluding the MEN loci, and recombination events narrowed the candidate region. Loss of heterozygosity studies in renal hamartomas, a jaw tumor, and a parathyroid tumor all pointed to the same 1q21-q32 region.

Now I'm examining the title and trying to figure out how to classify "Autosomal dominant primary hyperparathyroidism and jaw tumor syndrome" — whether this is a single coordinated disease name or distinct entities joined under one syndrome heading.

I'm weighing whether to mark "Autosomal dominant primary hyperparathyroidism and jaw tumor syndrome" as one composite span or split "Autosomal dominant" off as a modifier on "primary hyperparathyroidism" alone. Since the coordination joins two distinct disease names (hyperparathyroidism and jaw tumor syndrome) rather than a single fixed unit, I'm leaning toward annotating this as a Composite Mention.
